en.title: Gems, ghosts and GTA VI: the biggest video games for autumn 2026
en.description: There are juggernauts and indie gems aplenty for when the nights draw in, from an ingenious puzzle game to blockbusters such as Marvel’s Wolverine ...
en.fullContent:
There are juggernauts and indie gems aplenty for when the nights draw in, from an ingenious puzzle game to blockbusters such as Marvel’s Wolverine and Call of Duty
  See all of our unmissable autumn arts recommendations here

After 20 years away, Capcom’s hyper kinetic action adventure returns, pitting skilled samurai Miyamoto Musashi against hordes of warriors and demons in Edo-period Kyoto. Master the complex combat then prepare for flashing blades, disembodied limbs and geysers of spraying blood.
  4 September; PC, PS5, Switch 2, Xbox

Billed as the first ever 5D platformer, Screenbound has you navigating a 3D landscape while simultaneously playing an on-screen handheld console, which contains a 2D mirror world. Everything you do in one affects the other in mind-bending ways. The most ingenious puzzle game we’ve seen in a long time.
  10 September; PC, PS5, Xbox

The team behind the brilliant Marvel’s Spider-Man titles is back with a very different kind of hero. The open-world New York setting is gone in favour of a globe-trotting narrative following Logan on his quest to protect vulnerable mutants. The visuals are gorgeous, while the slick combat brings literal meaning to the term bleeding edge.
  15 September; PS5

The tactical role-playing adventure series returns to the realm explored in the acclaimed Fire Emblem: Three Houses. This time, hopeful contestants arrive at the glorious city of Dagsion to compete in a contest where the winner is granted a single wish. Deep combat, lush settings and fraught relationships are guaranteed.
   17 September; Switch 2

Silent Hill comes to the east coast of Scotland in a beautifully gloomy new horror adventure. You play as Simon Ordell, returning to a quiet harbour town with no memory of whatever catastrophe has taken place there. The place seems abandoned, but you are not alone for long …
  24 September; PC, PS5

en.title: 'More than just a cameo': New Wolverine video game features Squamish language, B.C. sites | CBC News
en.description: A sign featuring the Squamish Nation's language is on display in a new Wolverine video game that’s expected to draw millions of players globally.
en.fullContent:
A sign featuring the Squamish Nation's language is on display in a new Wolverine video game that’s expected to draw millions of players globally.

The game, Marvel’s Wolverine, will be released on Sept. 15 on PlayStation 5 and shows off several slices of B.C., including North Vancouver, the Lions Gate Bridge and the Sea-to-Sky Highway.

At one point, while the main character Logan (aka Wolverine) is driving a motorcycle along the highway, the Sḵwx̱wú7mesh sníchim (Squamish language) is displayed on two signs, spelling out the words for Whistler — Sk̲wik̲w — and Squamish — Sḵwx̱wú7mesh.

"It's something that I felt we absolutely had to do," said senior art director Gavin Goulden, who's based in Vancouver. "I worked with the team to get like the proper signage for it."

He said it was also critical to have real parts of Canada represented in the game, since Wolverine's character was born in Alberta.

"Wolverine is a Canadian hero, arguably the most famous Canadian superhero that there is," Goulden said.

en.title: This RPG Will Have You Exploring the Surreal Worlds of Hieronymus Bosch
en.description: Do you imagine yourself walking in The Garden of Earthly Delights?
en.fullContent:
Do you imagine yourself walking in The Garden of Earthly Delights?

Hieronymus is an action RPG that was announced at Future Games Show during Gamescom. It's a title that will let you explore the most iconic paintings by Hieronymus Bosch, who was a Dutch painter known for his surreal, fantastical artworks.

You'll play as Helena van Aken, and you'll use medieval weapons and alchemy to discover the secrets behind her family and their relation to otherworldly powers, while having the famous magician Dr. Georg Faustus as your companion.

The game will also allow you to visit the painter's house and use alchemy to stun creatures, lure them away, or influence their behavior and use them to your advantage.

The developers have shared on Twitter/X some of the creatures you'll find in the game. Check them out:

Seeing games inspired by or recreating famous paintings is not new, but one that could take you to Bosch's macabre depictions of hell sounds interesting and entertaining.

en.title: Upcoming games – September 2026
en.description: This September, guide four fates, explore beyond the storm wall, kick off The World’s Game, and more! Check out this selection of games launching s...
en.fullContent:
This September, guide four fates, explore beyond the storm wall, kick off The World’s Game, and more! Check out this selection of games launching soon on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch, and don’t forget to click on any that catch your eye for pre-orders, purchases or to add them to your Wish List.

184 AD, Later Han Dynasty China. The land is overcome by chaos and destruction, and the imperial dynasty that prospered for many years is on the verge of collapse. Become a nameless militia soldier fighting for survival against deadly demons and superhuman enemy warriors, using swordplay based on Chinese martial arts to awaken the true power within.

Grab a friend and launch into an intergalactic 2-player co-op adventure set in a wholly new retro anime world. Team up as Maki and Omura, two inseparable explorers with more determination than experience. Brave the perils of space in search of help for their crumbling station home, which is now trapped within a supernatural cosmic storm.

In this return of the iconic Capcom swordplay series, experience intense swordplay action and explore the historic Japanese capital of Edo-period Kyoto, twisted by malevolent clouds of Malice and demons called Genma. Through gritty, blood-soaked brawls, Miyamoto Musashi searches for his reason to fight. What fate awaits at the end of his path?

Craft powerful weapons, construct elaborate halls, and slay mighty foes to prove yourself to Odin! Discover an immersive procedurally-generated world, with different biomes that each feature distinct environments, unique resources and dangerous enemies. Become a Viking and sail the open seas in search of lands unknown, alone or with up to nine friends.

On RuneScape's forgotten continent of Ashenfall, dragons have awoken. Gather, build, and craft in this co-operative survival adventure, embarking on quests, levelling up your skills and exploring a beautiful, hand-crafted world. Only by mastering survival and uncovering ancient secrets can you hope to face the ferocious Dragon Queen…

en.title: Sony Reveals 2 PlayStation State of Plays for September 2026 — and They Are Happening on the Same Day
en.description: Sony has confirmed not one but two PlayStation State of Play presentations will air later this week.
en.fullContent:
Sony has confirmed not one but two PlayStation State of Play presentations will air later this week.

As part of a PlayStation.Blog post, the company revealed the first of the two showcases will start streaming this Thursday, September 3, at 6am PT / 9am ET / 3:00pm CEST / 10:00pm JST. It's promised to feature "updates and announcements from PlayStation Studios and our third-party partners" and will end with an "extended look at the vast world" of Square Enix's Final Fantasy 7 Revelation.

Then, immediately after the first show concludes, a State of Play Japan broadcast will begin. Attack on Titan and Octopath Traveler 0 voice actor Yuki Kaji has returned to host the show, which is said to "offer deep dives into upcoming games from game studios in Japan and Asia, including new gameplay, announcements, and more."

How long each show will be remains unclear, but we can already think of at least a few games that players are hoping to see. Social media feeds have already filled up with mentions of Naughty Dog and its long-awaited sci-fi game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. Nearly two years removed from its initial reveal, we've still seen very, very little from the studio's new IP. PlayStation players were already upset to see it absent from June's show, so let's hope the September State of Play gives fans at least a little something to hold onto.

Another game on the horizon is Insomniac Games' Marvel's Wolverine. The next installment in its line of superhero video games has a PS5 release date of September 15, a little less than two weeks from when the presentation is set to begin. That makes this week's show the perfect opportunity for Sony to get its claws firmly into any hesitant fans, even if there isn't much left to show.

What else can we expect? Well, outside of an even closer look at Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, it's somewhat of a mystery, but if all else fails, you can bet livestream chats will be brimming with at least one topic: physical games. Gaming fans have continued to surround PlayStation with calls for Sony to ditch its plan to kill physical disc support in January 2028, and this week's presentation will likely be no different.
